trust_decision.summary: For a client-facing ConfigService request, whether config may be served for appId X is decided by ClientAuthenticationFilter, which runs only on the servlet URL patterns registered in ConfigServiceAutoConfiguration (/configs/*, /configfiles/*, /notifications/v2/*), derives X from the servlet path or from the appId query parameter in AccessKeyUtil.extractAppIdFromRequest, and lets the request through whenever the AccessKey cache holds no FILTER-mode secret for that exact case-insensitive X.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'appId parsing and non-canonical matching', and extractAppIdFromRequest is the only place an appId is derived from the request for the access-key check; every route branch of the check funnels through it.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /notifications/v2 (exact path; the v2 long-poll endpoint of NotificationControllerV2 at NotificationControllerV2.java:67,99) - the fix adds the servlet pattern '/notifications/v2' at fix.diff:13 because '/notifications/v2/*' does not match the exact path
fix_sites.module_kind: spring auto-configuration / servlet filter registration (composition root)

fix_sites.where: fix.diff:50 (return validateAppId(appId) closing the branch chain at AccessKeyUtil.java:53-68)
fix_sites.entry_point: GET /configs/{appId}/{cluster}/{namespace} (ConfigController.java:94); GET /configfiles/{appId}/{cluster}/{namespace} (ConfigFileController.java:122); GET /configfiles/json/{appId}/{cluster}/{namespace} (ConfigFileController.java:140); GET /notifications/v2 (query param appId)
GET /configfiles/raw/{appId}/{cluster}/{namespace} (ConfigFileController.java:158) - before the fix the generic '/configfiles/' branch parsed the literal word 'raw' as the appId
all of the above - one shared canonical-appId gate reused by every extraction branch
fix_sites.module_kind: shared validator delegating to the apollo-common InputValidator schema

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: no second implementation, lower-level caller, wrapper or serialization path for this check exists: AccessKeyUtil is the only producer of an appId for access-key auth and ClientAuthenticationFilter is its only caller (grep of src/main for AccessKeyUtil / findAvailableSecret / Signature.signature)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The one route the published fix leaves unprotected is the deprecated v1 long-poll GET /notifications: it is annotated @Deprecated and documented as 'reserved for older version of apollo clients' (NotificationController.java:52-54,77-78), it takes appId from a query parameter rather than the path, and it returns only notification ids rather than configuration content - so a solver can argue it is a neighbouring legacy feature outside the advisory's config-content protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An app with no access keys (or only OBSERVER-mode keys) must keep being served without a signature: the filter is deliberately fail-open when the secret lookup is empty and OBSERVER mode only logs a bad signature (ClientAuthenticationFilter.java:73-86), and the docs state the mechanism applies only 'if the application has access keys enabled' (docs/en/portal/apollo-user-guide.md:555). The obvious over-hardening - answering 401 whenever no FILTER-mode secret is found - breaks every such client. Two neighbours reinforce it: the appId match is deliberately case-insensitive (AccessKeyServiceWithCache.java:84, changes-1.9.0.md:24), and the ApolloNoAppIdPlaceHolder / public-namespace route must stay open (ConfigController.java:118, WatchKeysUtil.java:104).

O6_input_shapes: appId with trailing whitespace in the path (/configs/mysql.example.test%20/default/application) - rejected by the new validator (fix.diff:182-189)
appId with non-ASCII / diacritic characters (/configs/mysql.exámple.test/default/application) - rejected (fix.diff:173-180)
the /configfiles/raw/{appId}/... path shape, where the old parser returned 'raw' as the appId (fix.diff:148-155)
the exact /notifications/v2 path, which the registered '/notifications/v2/*' pattern does not match (fix.diff:131-138)
the same non-canonical appId arriving through the appId query parameter on the notification route (fix.diff:191-199)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /notifications (v1 single-namespace long-poll, appId supplied as a request parameter) - no access-key filter is registered for this path at the pinned commit, and the published fix adds only the /notifications/v2 patterns
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: @Deprecated v1 protocol 'reserved for older version of apollo clients' that cannot compute an access-key signature; it leaks only notification ids/namespace activity, not configuration content, so it can be argued to be a legacy neighbour rather than part of the protected sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same Maven module, configservice/controller package, one file away from the v2 controller the fix reasons about; one package from the landing point (configservice/util)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new '/configfiles/<format>/...' branch (e.g. /configfiles/xml/{appId}/...) whose prefix is checked after the generic '/configfiles/' branch, so the format word becomes the appId
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix is exactly this shape for 'raw': the project keeps adding output formats to ConfigFileController, and the constants are a hand-maintained prefix list, so a maintainer adding a format/suffix route would plausibly forget the matching constant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second FilterRegistrationBean (or a second auto-configuration) registering ClientAuthenticationFilter for another pattern list, e.g. '/configfiles/v2/*' or '/appnamespaces/*', with its own exact-path gap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same file already hand-enumerates servlet patterns, and apollo-adminservice does the identical enumerate-patterns wiring for a different filter (AdminServiceAutoConfiguration.java:34-51); a new client-facing endpoint is normally added by adding one more addUrlPatterns line.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a wrapper/lower-level caller that takes an appId from a request parameter or a DTO field and calls findAvailableSecret(appId) directly, skipping extractAppIdFromRequest and therefore the canonical check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: findAvailableSecret/findObservableSecrets are public methods on a public @Component, so a maintainer adding a batch or internal lookup endpoint would naturally call them with the appId they already hold.

O9_family: Improper authentication / authentication bypass through non-canonical identifier matching (CWE-287) rooted in improper input validation of the appId (CWE-20)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module reactor (apollo-common, apollo-biz, apollo-configservice, apollo-adminservice, apollo-portal, apollo-assembly, ...), Spring Boot 2.7.11, JUnit 4 + Mockito + AssertJ; H2 2.2.220 in-memory for integration tests (pom.xml:64,67,80,107-115)
O10_build.project_tests: Unit: apollo-configservice/src/test/java/com/ctrip/framework/apollo/configservice/util/AccessKeyUtilTest.java, .../filter/ClientAuthenticationFilterTest.java, .../service/AccessKeyServiceWithCacheTest.java. Integration (embedded Tomcat + in-memory H2, apollo-configservice/src/test/resources/application.properties:19, Consul/Zookeeper disabled at :16-17): ConfigControllerIntegrationTest, ConfigFileControllerIntegrationTest, NotificationControllerV2IntegrationTest, NotificationControllerIntegrationTest. The fix adds a new ConfigServiceAutoConfigurationTest and four new AccessKeyUtilTest methods.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject or trim only the appId shape named in the report inside extractAppIdFromRequest (trim/lowercase, or reject only a trailing space) instead of gating every branch on the canonical appId schema, and fix only the route the report shows - leaving the exact /notifications/v2 path unregistered and the /configfiles/raw prefix still parsed as appId 'raw'; the second tempting step is to answer 401 whenever the secret cache is empty, which breaks every app without access keys.

out_of_scope_notes: apollo-adminservice has its own access-control filter with the same hand-enumerated URL-pattern shape (AdminServiceAuthenticationFilter, AdminServiceAutoConfiguration.java:34-51) but a shared admin token and a different sink; not part of this advisory and not pursued.
